title: Every activity states its rationale
statement: Before an activity goes in, write its rationale: the knowledge and performance it targets, the failure it guards against, why this activity, and when its support comes off.
detail: The general instruction rules a second-round review applied to the reading course say any activity needs a rationale: the target knowledge type, the performance, the failure mode it protects against, why this activity, and the condition for retiring its scaffold. The reading project's lesson-plan validator checks that every assessment item argues its format.
